Quick answer: Pressable is managed WordPress hosting owned by Automattic. Plans start at $250 a year for one site (about $20.83 a month, billed yearly) and every plan includes staging sites, a global CDN, daily file backups with hourly database backups, 24/7 support and a free Jetpack Security license. It is priced above budget hosts, so it suits businesses, online stores and agencies that want WordPress handled for them.

Key takeaways

  • Plans are sized by number of WordPress installs, monthly visits and storage, not by “unlimited” promises.
  • Every Signature plan includes Jetpack Security, which Pressable values at $239 a year.
  • Going over your visits or storage is billed: $1.20 per 1,000 visits and $1.00 per GB, per the pricing page.
  • There is a 30-day money-back guarantee, but no free trial.

What is Pressable?

Pressable is a managed WordPress host: it runs only WordPress, and handles server setup, caching, core updates, backups and security for you. It is part of Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, Jetpack and WooCommerce, and pitches itself mainly at agencies, WooCommerce stores and growing businesses.

Managed hosting costs more than shared hosting. You pay for performance, expert WordPress support and less time spent on maintenance. If you are new to hosting types, start with our guide to starting a WordPress website.

How much does Pressable cost?

These are the Signature plans on Pressable’s pricing page in November 2026, billed yearly (yearly billing shows “2 months free” compared with monthly):

Larger Signature plans (up to 100 installs) and custom Premium plans (from $350 a month, sales-led) are also listed. Monthly billing is available; the homepage showed the one-site plan at $25 a month. Each plan also includes the same number of staging and sandbox sites as installs.

Watch the overage fees. Usage above your plan’s visits and storage is billed at $1.20 per 1,000 visits and $1.00 per GB. Check your current monthly visits in your analytics before choosing a plan, and leave headroom for busy seasons.

What is included on every plan?

The Jetpack Security license is the stand-out value. If you would otherwise buy Jetpack backups and scanning separately, that cost is covered by the hosting plan. Our Jetpack review explains what it includes.

Performance and data centers

Each site runs with dedicated PHP workers (Pressable lists 5 per site on Signature plans) and automatic failover between a primary and secondary server. Its data-center help article lists four primary locations: Amsterdam, Washington DC, Los Angeles and Dallas. You choose one when you create a site and cannot change it later, so pick the one closest to most of your visitors. The global CDN serves cached pages and images from locations nearer your visitors.

Pressable pros and cons

Who is Pressable best for?

  • Agencies and freelancers managing several client sites from one dashboard. The multi-install plans and staging per site fit that workflow.
  • WooCommerce stores that need dependable performance and support. See our WooCommerce extensions guide for the store side.
  • Growing business sites that have outgrown shared hosting and want someone else to handle updates, caching and backups.

Who should skip it: a brand-new blog or hobby site with little traffic. A budget host is cheaper while you find your feet, and you can move later. Compare alternatives in our managed hosting comparison, our SiteGround review and our Hostinger review. If you would rather not manage hosting at all, WordPress.com bundles hosting into its plans.

How to move your site to Pressable

  1. Pick a plan with enough visits for your current traffic and the data center nearest your visitors.
  2. Request a free migration from Pressable’s team, or use its migration plugin.
  3. Test the copied site on its temporary URL: pages, forms, checkout and logins.
  4. Point your domain’s DNS to Pressable and confirm SSL is active.
  5. Connect Jetpack Security and confirm the first backup completes.

Our guide to moving a website to a new host covers each step and the checks that protect your search rankings.

FAQ

Is Pressable owned by Automattic?

Yes. Pressable is an Automattic company, alongside WordPress.com, Jetpack and WooCommerce.

Does Pressable have a free trial?

No standard free trial was listed when we checked. It offers a 30-day money-back guarantee instead.

Does Pressable include email?

No. Like most managed WordPress hosts, Pressable focuses on WordPress. Use a business email service; see our business email guide.

What happens if I go over my monthly visits?

Pressable bills overages: $1.20 per 1,000 visits and $1.00 per GB of storage above your plan, according to its pricing page. You can upgrade at any time.

Can I host WooCommerce on Pressable?

Yes. Pressable specifically markets its hosting to WooCommerce stores.

Verdict: is Pressable worth it?

Pressable is a solid pick if you want managed WordPress hosting from the company that builds WordPress.com, especially if you value having Jetpack Security, staging and expert support included. It costs more than budget hosting, and the visit-based limits mean you should size your plan carefully. For an established business site, store or agency it is worth shortlisting. Prices and features were checked on the vendors’ official pages in November 2026. They change, so confirm on the vendor’s site before you buy.
